notes: The audit row applies only to DELETE (unenroll), which calls writeAdminAudit for 'mfa_unenrolled'. POST (start enrollment) does NOT write an audit row — the 'mfa_enrolled' event is written by .../mfa/verify instead. GET/POST talk to Supabase Auth's MFA API (listFactors/enroll), not a raw table; admin_backup_codes is the only directly queried table. All three verbs require authMethod === 'session' (403 for admin_key/dev_bypass sentinels). POST projection is {factor_id, qr_code, secret, uri}; DELETE is {unenrolled:true}; the recorded projection is the GET shape. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: FINDINGS. (1) AUDIT ASYMMETRY: only DELETE writes admin_audit_log (:138). GET and POST write none — so starting an enrollment (a security-state-changing operation that mints a TOTP secret, :82-85) leaves no audit row; only the PostHog event at :96 records it, and that is best-effort (src/lib/admin/analytics.ts:112 returns early when POSTHOG_API_KEY is unset). (2) Audit failure is deliberately swallowed at :146-149 with the reason stated at :147; the response is still 200, so the caller cannot distinguish audited from unaudited. This is a documented choice, not an accident. (3) The TOTP `secret` and `qr_code` are returned in the response body at :104-105 — intentional per the header comment at :98-100, but it means the plaintext secret transits the envelope. (4) CENSUS DISAGREEMENT: the census lists census_reads [admin_backup_codes] and census_writes [admin_backup_codes, admin_audit_log] — all confirmed — but MISSES `profiles`, which every request reads through verifyAdminAuth (src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:117-120). It also misses the conditional admin_backup_codes SELECT/UPDATE inside the MFA gate (src/lib/admin/backup-codes.ts:116, :127), reachable only when ADMIN_MFA_ENFORCED='true'. (5) The TOTP factors themselves are NOT in this repo's Postgres — they live in Supabase GoTrue, reached via supabase.auth.mfa.* at :56, :82, :127; there is no local table for them. (6) No SELECT *. No verifyAdminAuth import. Its pipeline-freshness / chain-alias block duplicates pipelines/status/route.ts almost verbatim. Thirty-plus COUNT queries run in parallel, most wrapped in .catch(() => 0) so a missing table degrades a metric rather than failing the response. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: FINDINGS. (1) MISSING GUARD — the most exposed of my six: no verifyAdminAuth (imports :1-7), yet this route fans out ~38 queries across ~20 tables AND performs a WRITE (the reaper at :189). src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:9-11 mandates the call; only the presence-only middleware check (src/middleware.ts:115) stands in front of it. (2) The task brief's premise about the 7 engine_health_* logic variables is WRONG FOR THIS ROUTE: /api/admin/stats reads no logic variables at all (whole-file read; no logic_variables SQL, no resolver import). They are read by src/app/api/quality/route.ts (header :37-38, application :211-212), with names/defaults in src/lib/quality/types.ts:492-515. Their Zod bounds and on_invalid posture are UNRESEARCHED — see engine_health_logic_variables.bounds/on_invalid — because /api/quality is not one of my routes. (3) A WRITE HIDES INSIDE A 'QUERY' ROUTE: reapStaleRunningRows() at :189 UPDATEs pipeline_runs to status='failed' (src/lib/admin/reap-stale-runs.ts:26-28). Its only call site in src/ is this GET, so stale-run reaping happens only when a human loads the admin dashboard; and its failure is swallowed by an empty catch (src/lib/admin/reap-stale-runs.ts:38-40). (4) UNPARAMETERISED SQL INTERPOLATION at :102: `linked_confidence < ${COA_IDENTITY_LINK_MIN_CONFIDENCE}` splices a TS module constant (src/lib/coa/link-confidence.ts:17, value 0.85) straight into the SQL string. Not injectable today (compile-time numeric constant, no request input on this route), but it is the one string-built predicate here. (5) SILENT-DEGRADATION CLASS: 15 `.catch(() => [{count:'0'}])` swallows (:123-186) plus 6 block-level empty catches (:222, :280, :350, :367, :387, :406) mean a broken table renders as a plausible zero with no error signal, no logError, and no flag in the payload. Note the asymmetry — the first ~17 queries (:52-119) have NO .catch, so those failures 500 the whole route. (6) KNOWN GAP, COMMENT vs CODE: the comment block at :296-301 says the 3-status IN-list misses run-chain.js's 4th status 'deferred_to_full'. The CODE is at :317 — `status IN ('completed','completed_with_warnings','completed_with_errors')` — and indeed omits it, so a deferred chain reads as never-completed and therefore stale (:342-344). The comment's claim matches the code, but the comment is not the evidence; :317 is. (7) ENVELOPE DEVIATION: bare 38-key object at :413-461, bare {error} at :464-467 (see envelope.deviations). (8) NO SELECT * on this route. (9) CENSUS AGREES COMPLETELY: all 20 census_reads tables confirmed at the lines above, and census_writes [pipeline_runs] confirmed at :189 -> src/lib/admin/reap-stale-runs.ts:26. Two clarifications — the `pp` at :83/:138 and `pb` at :140 are ALIASES for permit_parcels and parcel_buildings, not tables; and the 16 table names inside the pg_class query (:398-401) and the PIPELINE_TABLE_MAP values behind the information_schema query (src/lib/admin/funnel.ts:836-865: permits, coa_applications, entities, address_points, parcels, building_footprints, neighbourhoods, wsib_registry, zoning_bylaw_areas, ravines, heritage_properties, toronto_centreline, permit_parcels, parcel_buildings, neighbourhood_storey_norms, neighbourhood_build_norms, permit_trades, cost_estimates, phase_calibration, phase_stay_calibration, data_quality_snapshots, pipeline_runs, engine

docs.purpose: Serves a live preview of the sales leads — from building permits and committee-of-adjustment applications — that a specific supplier account would see, based on that supplier's registered trade categories, so an admin can check or demo what a given supplier's feed looks like.
docs.data_story: It reads 5 tables — `suppliers`, `supplier_trades`, `trades`, `lead_trades` and `trade_forecasts` and writes nothing. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 12 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. **Nothing in this repository calls it.** That is the state this registry exists to make visible, not a claim that it is dead — a caller could be a bookmark, an external system, or a path built from variables.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `QUERY`. It declares its `database.reads[]` with named columns, its response projection as an explicit whitelist, its auth class, its rate bucket and its staleness — and `outputs.writes` is forced to `"none"`. Its `consumers[]` is the field that matters most here: today it is empty, and the orphan panel renders that as a red row rather than leaving it to be discovered years later.

programme.why: `/api/parcels/lookup` is the parcel product's only data contract: the consumer whitelist, the tier-stratified degradation and the entitlement gate all live here.

leakage.behaviour: Its entitlement check reads `entitlements` joined on `product = 'lead_gen'`, because `chk_entitlements_product` admits only `lead_gen` and `flight_center`. The parcel product has no key of its own in the live database — Spec 128 R-01 rules that it should, and the CHECK widening has not landed.

The parcel contract is built out of LEAD-GEN-NAMESPACED shared helpers: its response envelope and every error mapping come from `src/features/leads/api/envelope.ts` and `src/features/leads/api/error-mapping.ts`. Nothing is wrong with the behaviour — they are generic helpers — but a scope-A contract importing from `src/features/leads/**` means the parcel product cannot be extracted without dragging the lead-gen feature directory with it. The fix is a move to a shared module, not a rewrite.

docs.purpose: The list of lots a signed-in person has chosen to keep an eye on, and the way to stop keeping an eye on one. Reading gives back each lot’s address, how much can be built on it as of right, how much the Committee of Adjustment route could allow, and whether a CoA ruling has landed nearby recently. NOT BUILT YET — this descriptor is the specification the route and its table will be built against.
docs.data_story: It will read one new table, `user_tracked_lots`, which holds nothing but the fact that a person tracked a parcel — user, parcel, when, and the jurisdiction. Everything shown about the lot itself is joined from `parcels`, which the pipeline already produces. The "new nearby ruling" flag is not stored anywhere: it is derived per request from `coa_applications`, by asking whether a decided application shares the parcel’s neighbourhood inside a recent window. Writing is a single delete of the user’s own row.

The table is DEFINED here rather than written as a migration because migrations are the Backend domain and a different committer; the full column list, the unique constraint, the index and the RLS class are in `inputs.tables[0].evidence` so the migration can be written without re-deciding anything.

THE DERIVED FIELD. Of the three figures the surface shows, two are real columns (`parcels.max_buildable_gfa_sqm`, `parcels.max_newbuild_coa_gfa_sqm`) and the third — "new nearby CoA ruling" — HAS NO COLUMN ANYWHERE. It is derivable (`coa_applications` carries `decision`, `decision_date` and `neighbourhood_id`, and the lookup route already joins CoA by neighbourhood) but nothing computes it. It is therefore declared nullable, and the client renders `null` as "—" rather than "NO". The window is an unregistered tunable (see `config`).

NO REUSE OF THE LEAD-GEN SAVE PATH. `useSaveLead`, `admin_watchlist` and `/api/leads/save` are the lead-gen product’s machinery; OD5 forbids reaching for them here, which is why this is a new table and a new route rather than a second consumer of an existing one.

docs.purpose: Lets someone browse and filter Toronto building permits — by status, trade, cost range, ward or search text — with pagination and each permit's matched trade classifications attached. A special mode on the same endpoint instead returns upcoming committee-of-adjustment approvals that have not yet become a building permit, so users see construction leads before the permit itself exists.
docs.data_story: It reads 4 tables — `permits`, `permit_trades`, `trades` and `coa_applications` and writes nothing. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. It is called from 1 place: `web_dashboard`.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `QUERY`. It declares its `database.reads[]` with named columns, its response projection as an explicit whitelist, its auth class, its rate bucket and its staleness — and `outputs.writes` is forced to `"none"`. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

A 20-line handler whose entire body delegates to captureDataQualitySnapshot() in src/lib/quality/metrics.ts, which fans out roughly sixteen parallel counting queries across the listed tables and upserts one row per day into data_quality_snapshots (ON CONFLICT (snapshot_date) DO UPDATE). No in-repo caller found. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: THE CLASSIFICATION QUESTION (both line numbers): '/api/quality/refresh' appears in AUTHENTICATED_API_ROUTES at src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:122 and '/api/quality' appears in PUBLIC_PREFIXES at src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:75. classifyRoute tests AUTHENTICATED_API_ROUTES FIRST at route-guard.ts:165 and returns at :166; the PUBLIC_PREFIXES test is at :170. Because :166 returns, :170 is unreachable for this path — AUTHENTICATED WINS. So this route is NOT public, despite the task brief's premise. Consequence a reviewer must know: the handler carries NO in-handler auth (route.ts:9 takes no request and calls no guard), so authentication rests ENTIRELY on middleware ordering. If someone ever reorders those two branches, or adds a sibling like /api/quality/refresh-all (which would match only the public prefix), this write endpoint silently becomes anonymous. It is also UNAUTHENTICATED-EQUIVALENT in dev: src/middleware.ts:49-77 short-circuits every non-public route when isDevMode() (src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:33). Second finding: it is an unrestricted work trigger — any authenticated user (no admin check, no rate limit) can fire 16 parallel full-table aggregate queries (src/lib/quality/metrics.ts:25-42, Promise.all over COUNT(*)-class scans of permits/permit_trades/entities/coa_applications/permit_parcels/permit_inspections) and overwrite today's data_quality_snapshots row. The write is idempotent per day (ON CONFLICT (snapshot_date) DO UPDATE, metrics.ts:167) so it is not destructive across days, but it does let a non-admin rewrite the row /api/quality then serves publicly. Two branches match this exact path and the ORDER decides it. (1) AUTHENTICATED_API_ROUTES contains the exact string '/api/quality/refresh' (src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:122) and is tested at route-guard.ts:165 — `pathname === r` is true, so classifyRoute RETURNS 'authenticated' at route-guard.ts:166. (2) PUBLIC_PREFIXES contains '/api/quality' (route-guard.ts:75) and is tested at route-guard.ts:170 — `startsWith` would also be true, but line 170 is NEVER REACHED for this path because line 166 already returned. WHERE nonce=$1 AND expires_at > NOW() RETURNING user_id makes single use structural. Calls Stripe (customers.create, checkout.sessions.create) and reuses or persists a stripe_customer_id on user_profiles. Public by exact-path exception — the nonce is the credential, not a session. logic_variables is read by loadDefaultPriceId() for stripe_price_id_default. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: NONCE GUARD VERDICT: sound. Single-use is structural (one atomic DELETE...RETURNING, :126-129), expiry enforced in the same predicate (:127), and expired / consumed / never-existed are deliberately indistinguishable to the caller (one code+message, :94-97). Nonce values are randomUUID() v4 minted server-side (src/app/api/subscribe/session/route.ts:158) with a 15-min DB-default TTL (migrations/114:90) — not guessable in practice. WHAT AN ATTACKER WITH A GUESSED NONCE RECEIVES: only `{ url }` (:213) — a Stripe-hosted Checkout URL bound to the victim's Stripe Customer (:190-196). No user_id, email, profile row, or entitlement data is returned. The practical impact is that the attacker could pay for the victim's subscription and burn the victim's nonce (DoS of one checkout round-trip); they cannot read victim data through this response. SECOND FINDING: this route does NOT re-check `account_deleted_at` or entitlement status, while the minting route does (session/route.ts:103 FOR UPDATE, :119) — a nonce minted before a deletion still exchanges inside the 15-min window. Two concurrent exchanges race on the row delete and only one receives the RETURNING row. Residual hazard documented and accepted at :229-232: if the Stripe call fails AFTER the DELETE commits, the nonce is burned and the user must re-mint via /api/subscribe/session. Stripe Customer creation is made race-safe by the COALESCE write guard at :168 (the loser adopts the winner's stored id; its own just-created Customer is orphaned and unused). | Caching: none observed — no Cache-Control header, no `export const revalidate`/`dynamic` (full file read :1-239) | Other guards / classification: Single-use nonce IS the credential. notes: Also cites docs/specs/00-architecture/116_multi_product_architecture.md §4. Verifies the Stripe-Signature header against STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET before trusting any payload and enforces a 1MB body cap as a DoS guard on this public route. The dedup INSERT into stripe_webhook_events and the entitlements upsert run in one transaction so a provider retry cannot double-apply an event. The response body is the provider-required { received: true } shape, not the app's standard envelope. A safeLogError wrapper guarantees a logging failure can never roll back the dedup transaction, which would otherwise forge an infinite retry loop. consumers: [] is expected — the caller is Stripe itself, external to this repo. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: CLOSED SET OF HANDLED event.type VALUES (classifyEvent switch, :177-280) — 6 handled types plus a no-op default: (1) 'checkout.session.completed' :179 -> newStatus 'active', identity from client_reference_id ?? metadata.user_id (:194), product from session.metadata.product when it validates against PRODUCTS else the OD5 default (:190, :196-197, :424-428); (2) 'customer.subscription.created' :203 and (3) 'customer.subscription.updated' :204 -> newStatus via mapStripeSubStatus (:211; src/lib/stripe/client.ts:58-69: active->active, past_due->past_due, unpaid->expired, EVERYTHING ELSE INCLUDING 'canceled' -> null/no-op), price from items.data[0] (:217); (4) 'invoice.payment_succeeded' :224 -> 'active', resolveProductViaSubscription true (:238); (5) 'invoice.payment_failed' :241 -> 'past_due' (:244,:251); (6) 'customer.subscription.deleted' :254 -> 'expired' (:258) — the SOLE canonical access-revocation signal (:139-143, :207-210); (7) default :268-278 -> all-null outcome, dedup row committed, 200 no-op. COLUMN MUTATION ANSWER: this route mutates NO user_profiles column — user_profiles is READ ONLY (:384-387); the header states this explicitly at :371-373 and I verified it by reading all 503 lines. The entitlements columns it can write are the 8 listed in `writes`. TWO DEFECTS A REVIEWER MUST KNOW: (a) the safeLogError wrapper (:75-81) exists specifically so a throwing logger cannot roll back the dedup row and forge an infinite Stripe retry loop — but the logWarn calls at :439 and :445 run INSIDE that same transaction UNWRAPPED, as does resolvePriceProduct's logWarn (src/lib/entitlements/index.ts:317, :325) reached from :450; the stated fence is therefore incomplete. (b) the 413 check compares `rawBody.length` — a JavaScript string length in UTF-16 code units — against a constant named MAX_BODY_BYTES (:310-311), so multi-byte payloads are undercounted; and request.text() at :292 has already buffered the whole body before the check runs, so the cap does not bound peak memory (the comment at :306-309 concedes this). CENSUS AGREEMENT: matches exactly (reads entitlements + user_profiles + logic_variables; writes stripe_webhook_events + entitlements). | Idempotency: GUARDED — verdict: sound. The dedup INSERT (:337-342) and the entitlement upsert (:458) execute inside ONE withTransaction (:330), so (a) a concurrent Stripe retry that loses the ON CONFLICT race returns early at :343-348 and applies nothing, and (b) if the side effect throws, the dedup row rolls back WITH it and Stripe's retry can legitimately re-process. Three additional write-side fences live in the upsert's WHERE clause (src/lib/entitlements/index.ts:171-173): an out-of-order watermark keyed on Stripe's own event.created (route :457, NOT wall clock), a deletion fence (status IS DISTINCT FROM 'cancelled_pending_deletion'), and a superseded-subscription fence (non-'active' events apply only when stripe_subscription_id matches).
